title: From White Screen to Production Hardened
subtitle: A single visual roadmap for the 100+ decisions behind a fast, maintainable, secure Vue frontend.
takeaway: Speed is a system property. The three pillars are ordered: optimize what users feel first, then structure the code that keeps it fast, then close the doors that attackers use.
prompt: Read the story top to bottom. Each concept has one diagram, one plain-English takeaway and one copy-paste prompt.

title: Speed Is a Feature Users Feel Before They Measure
subtitle: Performance is not a Lighthouse score. It is a user deciding whether to stay, scroll or buy.
takeaway: A slow app loses attention before it loses arguments. Every optimization in this guide attacks one of four costs: bytes over the wire, JavaScript on the main thread, DOM work per render, or uncertainty in the UI.
prompt: Before changing code, open DevTools Network + Performance and name the bottleneck out loud. Never optimize by vibes.

title: The Pipeline: Optimize, Scale, Secure, Verify
subtitle: Three hardening pillars run in strict order, and a verification gate sits after each one.
takeaway: The order is deliberate: architecture changes can invalidate performance work, and security work can break auth flows. Sequential stages with tests between them make regressions visible instead of mysterious.
prompt: Follow /frontend-opt-tests → /scaling-tests → /security-tests. Do not start stage N+1 while stage N has a red test.

title: How to Read This Playbook in Ten Minutes
subtitle: Use it as a story, a visual glossary, or a prompt deck — each concept works on its own.
takeaway: A guide that cannot be scanned will not be used. The images are the table of contents; the prompts are the action; the tests are the proof.
prompt: Bookmark the chapter you are working on today and open the matching prompt from the Prompt Library section.

title: The Loop That Makes Optimization Repeatable
subtitle: Measure, locate, patch, verify, ship — then repeat. Optimization is a loop, not a one-off cleanup.
takeaway: A loop with one change per iteration gives you attribution: you know which edit moved LCP, which one broke reactivity, and which one to revert.
prompt: For every change, write the before number and the after number in the commit message. If you cannot measure it, call it a refactor, not a performance fix.

title: One Skill Per Session: The Token Budget Is Real
subtitle: Clear context, scope file reads, commit per phase — the same code with a tighter prompt costs far fewer tokens.
takeaway: Large contexts are slow and expensive. The guide's four-phase prompt split exists because focused prompts produce better edits, cleaner checkpoints and lower token bills.
prompt: Run /clear between phases, pin exact paths with @src/views/Dashboard.vue, and commit after every phase.

title: Separation of Concerns
subtitle: A view renders, a composable decides, a service fetches. When those jobs stay apart, each can change alone.
takeaway: Mixed concerns make every edit risky. Splitting by job, not by file type, is the first move in every refactor.
prompt: Split this component into a presentational view, one use<Feature> composable and one typed service call.

title: Single Source of Truth
subtitle: One authoritative value per fact. Every screen reads the same value instead of keeping a private copy.
takeaway: Copying server data into local state creates drift. Read the canonical store and derive everything else.
prompt: Find local copies of server data in this component and replace each with a store getter or query result.

title: Unidirectional Data Flow
subtitle: State flows down as props, events flow up as intent. The direction never reverses.
takeaway: Two-way mutation across sibling components hides causality. Events up, state down keeps every change explainable.
prompt: Replace this child's direct state mutation with an emit to its parent and one store action.

title: Prop Drilling
subtitle: Passing a value through five components that do not use it adds noise and coupling at every hop.
takeaway: Drilling is not always wrong — one level is explicit and cheap. It becomes a smell when pass-through props outnumber real props.
prompt: Replace this 3+ level prop chain with provide/inject scoped to the feature or a store getter.

title: State Mutation
subtitle: Mutating shared state in place hides the moment of change. Replace the object so the change is visible and traceable.
takeaway: In-place mutation breaks shallow reactivity and memoization because nothing detects a new identity.
prompt: Convert this nested mutation into a single immutable reassignment of the top-level value.

title: Derived State
subtitle: If a value can be computed from existing state, do not store it. Derive it and let caching do the work.
takeaway: Derived state stored in a ref needs a watcher to stay correct. computed() makes correctness structural.
prompt: Replace this ref + watcher pair with computed() and delete the synchronized copy.

title: Reactive Coupling
subtitle: When one render touches unrelated reactive values, every unrelated change re-renders it. Narrow the dependency.
takeaway: Reactivity is a dependency graph. The bigger the graph each component subscribes to, the more work every update causes.
prompt: Split this shared reactive object into focused refs and read only the field each component needs.

title: Side Effects
subtitle: Fetching, timers, logging and analytics are effects. Give them a named home and a cleanup path.
takeaway: Effects scattered in templates and computed getters run unpredictably and are hard to cancel.
prompt: Move this effect into the composable, attach onScopeDispose, and return a cancel function.

title: Composable Extraction
subtitle: When a component mixes state, Effects and markup, extract the behaviour into use<Feature>() and leave the view declarative.
takeaway: Composables are the Vue unit of reusable stateful logic. They keep business rules out of templates and out of global stores.
prompt: Extract this component's fetch + filter + reset logic into use<Feature>.ts and keep only bindings in the view.

title: Reactivity Leaks
subtitle: A proxy nested inside a plain wrapper can silently lose reactivity — or keep tracking long after it is needed.
takeaway: Deep reactivity is convenient for small objects and expensive for large ones. Leaks also happen when tracking outlives the component.
prompt: Audit this file for reactive() around third-party instances and narrow it with shallowRef or markRaw.

title: Watcher Abuse
subtitle: A watcher that recomputes, re-fetches and re-writes state is usually a computed, an effect or an event in disguise.
takeaway: Watchers are for crossing boundaries: state → network, state → storage. Use computed for values.
prompt: Replace this watcher: move derived work to computed, narrow dependencies, and keep only the side effect.

title: Memory Leaks
subtitle: Listeners, timers and subscriptions that outlive a component keep the whole tree alive in memory.
takeaway: Leaks are invisible in development and fatal after a hundred route changes. Cleanup is part of the feature, not an afterthought.
prompt: Add teardown for every listener/timer/subscription created in this component and verify with the heap profiler.

title: Template Bloat
subtitle: Thousands of nodes and inline expressions make the renderer do work on every update.
takeaway: Vue's renderer is fast, but it still walks every node. Shrink the tree first, then optimize the diff.
prompt: Virtualize this list and move the inline formatting calls into a computed map before touching reactivity.

title: Type Safety
subtitle: Types move whole classes of bugs from runtime to editor time — especially at API and prop boundaries.
takeaway: Type safety is not ceremony; it is the cheapest regression test you run on every keystroke.
prompt: Type this component's props and its service response, then run vue-tsc and fix the reported errors.

title: God Component
subtitle: One component that fetches, decides, formats and renders every state becomes impossible to reason about or reuse.
takeaway: Large components concentrate coupling. The goal is not tiny files for their own sake but small reasons to change.
prompt: List the reasons this component changes and split it along those boundaries into child views and composables.

title: Presentational Components
subtitle: A dumb component receives data and emits events. It has no store, no fetching and no knowledge of the app.
takeaway: Presentational components are easy to test, storybook and reuse because they have no hidden dependencies.
prompt: Remove store imports from this widget and pass the required data and callbacks as props/emits instead.

title: Container Components
subtitle: The container knows where data comes from; the children only know how to display it.
takeaway: The container/presentational split localizes app knowledge so the expensive UI tests can stay shallow.
prompt: Move this page's store reads and fetch calls into a container and leave the markup in a props-only child.

title: High Cohesion
subtitle: Code that changes for the same reason lives together. That is what a feature folder really means.
takeaway: Cohesion reduces merge conflicts and makes ownership obvious because one domain is one place.
prompt: Move this feature's view, composable, API module and types into src/features/<domain>/.

title: Low Coupling
subtitle: Components should depend on narrow interfaces, not on each other's internals.
takeaway: Low coupling is what makes parallel work possible: teams can change their own code without coordinating every edit.
prompt: Replace this component's import of a sibling's internals with a typed service call or emitted event.

title: Composition over Inheritance
subtitle: Vue components compose through slots and props. Deep component inheritance creates fragile, hidden behaviour.
takeaway: Composition makes data flow visible. Inheritance hides it in a chain you have to reconstruct mentally.
prompt: Replace this component inheritance with a wrapper component using slots plus a shared composable.

title: Immutability
subtitle: Treat state snapshots as values. A new reference means something changed; the same reference means nothing did.
takeaway: Immutability is the contract that makes memoization, shallow reactivity and time-travel debugging work.
prompt: Rewrite this state change as a top-level reassignment and verify the memoized child still updates.

title: Dependency Injection
subtitle: Supply dependencies from outside instead of constructing them inside. The consumer stays testable and swappable.
takeaway: Hard-coded imports bind a component to one implementation. Injection lets tests replace it without mocking modules.
prompt: Provide this API client at the feature root and inject it into the composable instead of importing it directly.

title: Inversion of Control
subtitle: Frameworks call your code. Let Vue own the lifecycle and keep your logic in hooks it can schedule and tear down.
takeaway: Fighting the scheduler produces double renders and race conditions. Hooks are the contract for when code runs.
prompt: Replace this manual DOM polling with a watcher/computed and move cleanup into onScopeDispose.

title: Event-Driven Architecture
subtitle: Events describe what happened. Producers do not need to know who reacts, which keeps features independent.
takeaway: Events decouple producers from consumers, but untyped global buses become invisible spaghetti. Keep the contract typed.
prompt: Replace this cross-feature callback chain with a typed event or store action and document its consumers.

title: State Machines
subtitle: Model UI as explicit states and allowed transitions. Impossible states become unrepresentable.
takeaway: Explicit states remove the impossible combinations that cause blank screens and double submissions.
prompt: Replace these booleans with a discriminated union status and render one branch per state.

title: Optimistic UI
subtitle: Apply the expected result immediately, then reconcile with the server. The interface feels instant.
takeaway: Optimistic UI trades a moment of uncertainty for a much faster feel. It is only safe when failures are handled visibly.
prompt: Apply this mutation optimistically, keep the previous snapshot, and roll back with a clear message on failure.

title: Race Conditions
subtitle: Two requests for the same query can return out of order. The slower, older answer must not win.
takeaway: Async results arriving in the wrong order is the classic source of stale search results and flickering UI.
prompt: Abort the previous request in this watcher or tag each response with a token and ignore stale results.

title: Idempotency
subtitle: Repeating the same operation must produce the same result. Retries then become safe instead of dangerous.
takeaway: Anything that can be retried will be retried. Design the mutation so the second attempt is harmless.
prompt: Attach an idempotency key to this mutation and disable the submit control while the request is pending.

title: Caching Strategy
subtitle: Every piece of data needs an owner and a lifetime: server cache, client store, or no cache at all.
takeaway: Cache policy is a design decision, not a library default. Wrong layers cause stale screens or needless requests.
prompt: Classify this data as server or client state, assign one cache owner, and document its staleness window.

title: Stale-While-Revalidate
subtitle: Show cached data instantly, refresh it quietly in the background, then replace it when the new answer arrives.
takeaway: SWR improves perceived speed without sacrificing freshness, because the refresh happens after paint.
prompt: Configure this query to return cached data immediately and refetch on mount and focus.

title: Code Splitting
subtitle: Ship the code for the current screen, not the whole app. Smaller entry chunks mean faster first paint.
takeaway: The browser must download, parse and execute everything you send. The cheapest byte is the one you never ship.
prompt: Convert this route or heavy feature to a dynamic import and inspect the new chunk graph.

title: Lazy Loading
subtitle: Defer a module until the user is likely to need it. Loading is a scheduling decision.
takeaway: Lazy loading without a fallback feels broken. Always render a placeholder that occupies the final space.
prompt: Wrap this heavy view in defineAsyncComponent with a skeleton loadingComponent and an errorComponent.

title: Tree Shaking
subtitle: The bundler drops exports nothing imports. Write code that can be dropped — keep side effects explicit.
takeaway: Tree shaking works best with static imports, named exports and pure modules. Wildcard imports defeat it.
prompt: Replace wildcard imports in this file with named imports and confirm the chunk shrinks after build.

title: Bundle Bloat
subtitle: Bloat is what happens when nobody owns the size budget. It creeps in one convenient import at a time.
takeaway: Size is a product constraint like any other. Without a budget, every dependency looks free until the Lighthouse score drops.
prompt: Run the bundle visualizer, find the largest module, and either lazy-load it or replace it.

title: Render Bottlenecks
subtitle: A bottleneck is a render that happens too often, touches too much, or does too much work per node.
takeaway: Render cost is (number of nodes) × (number of renders) × (work per node). Attack whichever factor is largest.
prompt: Profile this interaction, name the re-rendering component, and apply one of the three fixes before moving on.

title: Virtual Scrolling
subtitle: Render the 20 rows the user can see, not the 10,000 rows the data contains.
takeaway: The DOM is the render bottleneck. Virtual scrolling caps it with a window and spacer elements.
prompt: Replace this v-for with @tanstack/vue-virtual and keep a fixed row height or measured estimate.

title: Debouncing
subtitle: Wait for a pause in the event stream before running the expensive work. Ideal for search input.
takeaway: Typing 'keyboard' should not fire seven requests. Debouncing collapses a burst into one intentional action.
prompt: Wrap this search handler in useDebounceFn(fn, 300) and cancel it on unmount.

title: Throttling
subtitle: Run at most once per interval. Ideal for continuous events like scroll, resize and pointer move.
takeaway: Throttling keeps feedback responsive without doing layout work on every native event.
prompt: Throttle this scroll/resize handler to one call per frame and read layout only inside that callback.

title: Error Boundaries
subtitle: Catch a child's render error locally and show a fallback. One broken widget should not blank the app.
takeaway: Error boundaries turn a total outage into a degraded feature. They belong around independent feature roots.
prompt: Wrap this feature view in an ErrorBoundary component with a retry button and error reporting hook.

title: Graceful Degradation
subtitle: Build for capable browsers, then define what the page does when a feature is missing or a request fails.
takeaway: Degradation is a product decision made in code: what is the minimum useful version of this screen?
prompt: Define the fallback for this feature when its API fails and render it without blocking the rest of the page.

title: Defensive Programming
subtitle: Validate at trust boundaries and assume partial data. Do not sprinkle checks through rendering code.
takeaway: Defensive code belongs at the edges. Inside the system, types and invariants should already hold.
prompt: Add a Zod schema at this service boundary and give the template a safe default for missing fields.

title: Strict Typing
subtitle: strict: true turns implicit assumptions into compiler errors. It is the cheapest long-term maintenance win.
takeaway: Strict mode pays back on every refactor: the compiler finds the callers you forgot.
prompt: Enable strict in tsconfig, run vue-tsc, and fix the errors in one domain at a time.

title: Interface Segregation
subtitle: Expose small, purpose-built interfaces instead of one giant catch-all type or store.
takeaway: Large interfaces force components to depend on fields they never use, which increases coupling and test cost.
prompt: Replace this catch-all type with two narrow interfaces named after their consumers.

title: Technical Debt
subtitle: Debt is the gap between the code you have and the code you wish you had. Interest is paid on every change.
takeaway: Debt becomes dangerous when nobody knows it exists. Write the limit down next to the shortcut.
prompt: Log each shortcut with a one-line limit and upgrade condition, then pay the highest-interest one first.

title: Refactoring
subtitle: Change the structure without changing behaviour. Tests are the safety net that makes this boring.
takeaway: Refactoring is a disciplined loop, not a week-long rewrite. Small steps with green tests keep risk near zero.
prompt: Add a test around this behaviour, then apply one structural change and re-run it before continuing.

title: Modularity
subtitle: Modules hide their internals behind a public surface. You can replace one without rewriting the app.
takeaway: A public index.ts is a cheap enforceable boundary: it tells you exactly what the rest of the app may use.
prompt: Add an index.ts to this feature and update imports to use the public surface only.

title: Scalability
subtitle: A scalable frontend grows by adding isolated features, not by making one giant app more complicated.
takeaway: Micro-frontends solve organizational problems. Start with module boundaries and shared conventions before adopting them.
prompt: Draw the ownership boundary for this feature and list the shared contracts it depends on.

title: Maintainability
subtitle: Maintainable code is easy to understand on the first read and safe to change on the tenth.
takeaway: Maintainability is the compound result of the other foundations — not a separate activity at the end.
prompt: Score this module on these six points and fix the weakest one with a single scoped change.

title: Abstraction Layers
subtitle: Each layer solves one problem and talks only to its neighbours. Leaks across layers create hidden coupling.
takeaway: Layers are useful only when they are enforced. One leaked import collapses the benefit of all of them.
prompt: Move this HTTP call out of the view into the service layer and keep only a typed result in the component.

title: Lifecycle Management
subtitle: Every resource has a birth, a working life and a teardown. Vue gives you hooks; use them symmetrically.
takeaway: Unmatched lifecycles are the root of timers firing after unmount and subscriptions piling up in long sessions.
prompt: Audit this component: pair every listener, timer and subscription with a teardown in onScopeDispose.

title: Phase 1 Overview: Bundle, Build & Route Splitting
subtitle: Seven levers decide how many bytes arrive and how much JavaScript the browser must parse before first paint.
takeaway: This phase touches configuration, not business logic. That makes it the safest place to start and easiest to measure.
prompt: Analyze package.json, vite.config.*, index.html and src/router/* only. Do not scan unrelated component files yet.

title: Convert Static Routes to Lazy Routes
subtitle: A static import puts every page in the entry bundle. A dynamic import gives each route its own chunk.
takeaway: Route-level splitting is the highest leverage change in most Vue apps: one line per route, immediate payload win.
prompt: Convert every static route component import in src/router/* to a dynamic () => import(...) import.

title: What dynamic import() Actually Returns
subtitle: import() is a promise of a module. The router understands a function returning that promise as an async component.
takeaway: Understanding the promise contract explains why typeof route.component === 'function' is the test for lazy routes.
prompt: Verify each route component is a function, not an imported object, and add a loading fallback for slow networks.

title: Vite manualChunks: Split Vendors Deliberately
subtitle: Vendor libraries change less often than app code. Separate chunks let returning users keep the cached parts.
takeaway: Chunking improves caching, not total bytes. Split heavy libraries that change independently of your app code.
prompt: Configure build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks in vite.config.* to isolate vue, vue-router, pinia and chart libraries.

title: Tree-Shaking at Build Time
subtitle: ES modules let Rollup delete unused exports. Side effects and wildcard imports keep dead code alive.
takeaway: Clean named imports are free performance: the bundler removes code you never call.
prompt: Replace wildcard imports in this module with named imports and confirm unused exports disappear from the build.

title: CSS Purging & Minification
subtitle: Ship the selectors you use. An unused design-system stylesheet can be larger than the app's JavaScript.
takeaway: CSS is render-blocking. A smaller stylesheet means the browser can paint sooner.
prompt: Enable CSS minification and purging in vite.config.*, and safelist any dynamically built class names.

title: Brotli & Gzip Compression
subtitle: Text assets compress extremely well. Let the CDN or Vite plugin serve a much smaller payload with the same bytes of meaning.
takeaway: Compression is the cheapest speed win available: no code changes, no risk, large transfer savings.
prompt: Add vite-plugin-compression for Brotli/Gzip and verify Content-Encoding: br on the built assets.

title: Preload Critical Assets
subtitle: Tell the browser about the font or entry chunk it will need immediately, instead of letting it discover them late.
takeaway: Preloading fixes discovery delay, not download size. Use it for the one or two assets on the critical path.
prompt: Add <link rel="preload"> for critical above-the-fold fonts and entry assets in index.html.

title: Vite Bundle Analyzer
subtitle: A picture of the build output turns 'the bundle feels big' into 'this library is 480 KB'.
takeaway: The analyzer is the measuring instrument for this entire phase. It tells you which lever is worth pulling.
prompt: Add rollup-plugin-visualizer configured to emit stats.html, then run npm run build and inspect the largest chunk.

title: Web Workers: Off the Main Thread
subtitle: Move heavy parsing and computation to a worker so scrolling and input stay responsive.
takeaway: A 300 ms parse on the main thread is a 300 ms freeze. In a worker it is invisible to the user.
prompt: Move this heavy parse/filter into a Vite module worker and post the result back as a plain object.

title: Bundle Budgets as a Guardrail
subtitle: A budget makes size a build failure instead of a surprise discovered in production.
takeaway: Budgets stop regression by one dependency at a time — exactly how bloat actually arrives.
prompt: Set build.chunkSizeWarningLimit and add a CI step that fails when the entry or vendor chunk exceeds the budget.

title: Phase 2 Overview: Heavy Component & List Rendering
subtitle: Five levers keep the DOM small and the renderer idle: async components, KeepAlive, virtualization, v-once and v-memo.
takeaway: Rendering work is bounded by the number of nodes and how often they are touched. This phase shrinks both numbers.
prompt: Identify the heaviest views, modals and large lists in src/views and src/components. Skip small UI primitives.

title: defineAsyncComponent for Heavy Widgets
subtitle: A modal, chart or rich editor that opens rarely should not be in the initial bundle at all.
takeaway: Async components convert a permanent download cost into a one-time cost paid only by users who open the feature.
prompt: Wrap each heavy conditional modal, drawer, editor and chart with defineAsyncComponent and a skeleton fallback.

title: KeepAlive for Stateful Views
subtitle: When users switch tabs often, unmounting and rebuilding the view wastes work and loses scroll/filter state.
takeaway: KeepAlive trades a bounded amount of memory for instant tab switching and preserved state — a good deal for navigation.
prompt: Wrap dynamic tab/route views in <KeepAlive :max="5"> and pause timers in onDeactivated.

title: Virtual Scrolling Implementation
subtitle: A virtualizer measures a scroll container, renders a window of rows and pads the rest with spacers.
takeaway: The virtualizer keeps DOM size constant, so scrolling a million rows costs the same as scrolling one hundred.
prompt: Replace this 100+ item v-for with @tanstack/vue-virtual using a fixed row height where possible.

title: v-once: Render Once, Skip Forever
subtitle: Static blocks never need a diff. v-once tells Vue to render them once and skip future updates entirely.
takeaway: v-once is the cheapest memoization: no dependencies to track, no comparisons to make.
prompt: Add v-once to template blocks whose content never changes after the first render, then verify with Devtools.

title: v-memo: Cache an Expensive Subtree
subtitle: Give Vue a list of primitive dependencies. The subtree re-renders only when one of them changes.
takeaway: v-memo is surgical: it avoids diff work for rows whose visible inputs did not change.
prompt: Add v-memo="[...]" to expensive v-for items using only primitive keys such as item.id and item.selected.

title: Layout Thrashing Prevention
subtitle: Reading layout after writing styles forces the browser to recalculate synchronously, again and again in a loop.
takeaway: Alternating reads and writes inside a loop turns one layout pass into N synchronous passes.
prompt: Batch layout reads before writes in this loop and move style writes into a requestAnimationFrame callback.

title: Reflow Elimination
subtitle: Some properties only repaint; others invalidate layout for the whole subtree. Prefer the cheaper ones.
takeaway: A reflow recalculates positions for descendants. Compositor-only properties skip that work entirely.
prompt: Change this animation from width/top to transform and verify in Devtools Rendering paint flashing.

title: GPU Compositing: transform & opacity
subtitle: transform and opacity can be handled by the compositor without running layout or paint on the main thread.
takeaway: The compositor is a separate thread that can move pre-painted layers. Feed it properties it understands.
prompt: Replace these position/size animations with transform and opacity, then record a Performance trace.

title: The 16.7ms Frame Budget
subtitle: At 60fps the browser has about 16.7 ms for JavaScript, style, layout, paint and compositing — together.
takeaway: Smoothness is a budget, not a feeling. Measure a frame trace and keep your JavaScript share small.
prompt: Record a Performance trace of this interaction and reduce the longest task to under 10ms.

title: Hardware Acceleration
subtitle: Browsers promote selected elements to GPU layers. The trick is choosing the few elements that benefit.
takeaway: Too many promoted layers make things worse. Promote during motion, then remove the hint.
prompt: Apply will-change: transform only to the animating element and remove it after transitionend.

title: CSS Containment: contain: content
subtitle: Containment tells the browser this subtree cannot affect layout or paint outside its box.
takeaway: In large dashboards, containment reduces the scope of invalidation from the page to one widget.
prompt: Add contain: content to independent dashboard widgets that have explicit dimensions.

title: Skeleton Screens
subtitle: A shaped placeholder communicates progress and reserves space, so the layout does not jump when data arrives.
takeaway: Skeletons do not make data faster; they make waiting legible and prevent layout jumps.
prompt: Add a skeleton loadingComponent to this async view with the same dimensions as the final content.

title: Progressive Hydration
subtitle: Server-rendered HTML is visible immediately; hydration attaches interactivity feature by feature instead of all at once.
takeaway: Full-app hydration can block the main thread even when the page already looks ready. Progressive hydration spreads the cost.
prompt: Evaluate hydrating only this page's interactive islands first; defer below-the-fold widgets to idle time.

title: Profile Renders Before Guessing
subtitle: Vue Devtools shows which components rendered and how long each took. Start there, not with a favorite directive.
takeaway: Measurement prevents cargo-cult optimization: v-once on a fast block changes nothing, while virtualizing a list changes everything.
prompt: Record one interaction in Vue Devtools, name the most expensive component, and apply one targeted fix.

title: Phase 3 Overview: Reactivity & Events
subtitle: Five changes reduce how often code runs: shallow reactivity, computed caching, targeted watchers, debounce and throttle.
takeaway: Reactivity is invisible until it is excessive. This phase narrows dependencies and controls event frequency.
prompt: Audit <script setup> blocks and Pinia stores in src/stores/* for reactivity and event bottlenecks only.

title: shallowRef for Large or External Objects
subtitle: shallowRef tracks only .value replacement. Perfect for big API arrays and third-party instances.
takeaway: Deep proxies cost memory and tracking time. If you always replace the whole object, shallowRef is strictly cheaper.
prompt: Replace ref/reactive with shallowRef for large read-only API arrays and third-party instances, using .value reassignment.

title: shallowReactive for Flat Shapes
subtitle: Make only root-level properties reactive when nested objects are treated as opaque values.
takeaway: shallowReactive keeps the familiar object API while avoiding deep proxy conversion on large nested data.
prompt: Convert this large reactive object to shallowReactive and replace nested objects instead of mutating them.

title: computed Caching Over Template Calls
subtitle: A method call in a template runs on every render. A computed runs only when its dependencies change.
takeaway: Moving work out of the template turns 'run every render' into 'run when inputs change'.
prompt: Replace expensive function calls in this template with computed properties and verify caching in a test.

title: Replace Deep Watchers With Targeted Getters
subtitle: deep: true walks the whole nested tree on every change. Watch the exact field you actually care about.
takeaway: A deep watcher on a large object is both broad and expensive. Targeted getters make intent obvious.
prompt: Replace watch(..., { deep: true }) in this file with getters for the specific nested properties.

title: Debounce Search Inputs
subtitle: One request after the user stops typing beats seven requests for seven keystrokes.
takeaway: Debouncing reduces network load and render churn while preserving the feeling of instant feedback in the input itself.
prompt: Add a 300ms debounce to this search/filter handler and cancel it when the component unmounts.

title: Throttle Scroll & Resize Handlers
subtitle: Native scroll and resize fire far faster than a frame. Throttle to one callback per animation frame.
takeaway: Throttling keeps visual feedback smooth without saturating the main thread with redundant work.
prompt: Throttle this scroll/resize handler to one call per frame and remove the listener on unmount.

title: Fixing Async Race Conditions
subtitle: When a newer request starts, cancel the older one — or tag results so stale answers can be discarded.
takeaway: A stale response overwriting a fresh one looks like a random bug. Cancellation makes ordering deterministic.
prompt: Add AbortController to this watcher-driven fetch and abort the previous request before starting the next.

title: Idempotent Actions & Retries
subtitle: A retried mutation must not create a second order. Pair a client lock with a server-side key.
takeaway: Client-side guards reduce accidents; only a server-side key makes retries genuinely safe.
prompt: Add a pending guard and an idempotency key to this mutation before enabling automatic retries.

title: Fixing Reactivity Leaks
subtitle: A memoized child that never updates usually means a shallow reference was mutated instead of replaced.
takeaway: Switching to shallowRef without switching to immutable updates is the most common cause of 'broken reactivity' reports.
prompt: Audit shallowRef usages for in-place mutation and convert each to a top-level reassignment.

title: Watcher Cleanup & stopHandle
subtitle: Watchers created inside effects can outlive the scope that made them. Keep them tied to a scope or stop them explicitly.
takeaway: Cleanup hooks are part of the watcher, not an optional courtesy — they prevent duplicated side effects over time.
prompt: Register onCleanup and onScopeDispose for every watcher in this composable that subscribes to an external source.

title: Fixing Memory Leaks
subtitle: After repeated navigation, heap size should return to baseline. If it grows, something still holds a reference.
takeaway: Leaks rarely show up in tests; they show up after a user has been in the app for an hour.
prompt: Add teardown for every listener/timer in this component and verify the heap across three mount cycles.

title: Fixing Template Bloat
subtitle: When every row has inline expressions and deeply nested branches, even small state changes re-render the whole area.
takeaway: Template expressions execute in the render context. Removing them reduces per-render allocations and diff complexity.
prompt: Move the formatting calls in this template into a computed map and memoize the rows on primitive keys.

title: Phase 4 Overview: Media & Rendering Architecture
subtitle: Images usually dominate payload, while SSR/SSG decisions dominate First Contentful Paint and SEO.
takeaway: This phase changes bytes and architecture, not state. Keep it separate from reactivity work to avoid confusion.
prompt: Scan templates and public/ / src/assets/ for image usage and check whether this project requires SSR/SSG.

title: Image Optimization Checklist
subtitle: Resizing, compressing and lazy-loading images usually removes more bytes than every JavaScript tweak combined.
takeaway: Images are often 60-80% of transferred bytes. A single unoptimized hero can outweigh the entire app bundle.
prompt: Audit oversized images in public/ and src/assets/, then resize and convert them to WebP/AVIF with fallbacks.

title: WebP & AVIF Formats
subtitle: Modern codecs deliver the same visual quality at much smaller sizes than JPEG/PNG.
takeaway: Format conversion is a pure payload win with no behavioural risk, so it belongs early in the media phase.
prompt: Update this image reference to prefer .avif/.webp with a JPEG fallback, or add vite-imagetools to the build.

title: Lazy-Load Below-the-Fold Images
subtitle: Browsers can defer off-screen images natively — no JavaScript observer needed for most cases.
takeaway: Native lazy loading removes off-screen network pressure from the critical path with one attribute.
prompt: Add loading="lazy", decoding="async" and explicit width/height to every below-the-fold tag.

title: Explicit Dimensions Prevent CLS
subtitle: Without width and height, the browser cannot reserve space. Late images push content down and cause layout shift.
takeaway: Cumulative Layout Shift is a Core Web Vital and a trust problem: users click the wrong thing when content moves.
prompt: Add width and height (or aspect-ratio) to every image that lacks them and measure CLS again.

title: fetchpriority for the Hero Image
subtitle: Not all images are equal. Tell the browser which one is the LCP element so it stops competing with below-the-fold assets.
takeaway: Priority hints make the browser's download queue match your product's visual hierarchy.
prompt: Mark the hero/LCP image eager with fetchpriority="high" and keep all gallery images lazy.

title: SSR: HTML on the First Response
subtitle: Server-side rendering sends meaningful HTML immediately, so users and crawlers see content before JavaScript runs.
takeaway: SSR is a trade: faster first paint and crawlability in exchange for infrastructure and hydration work.
prompt: Assess this route's SEO/FCP needs and list the server requirements before considering an SSR migration.

title: SSG: Render Once at Build Time
subtitle: For content that rarely changes, pre-render at build time and serve static HTML from a CDN.
takeaway: SSG gives SSR-like first paint with none of the per-request rendering cost, as long as content is build-time data.
prompt: Identify statically known routes here and recommend prerendering them instead of full SSR.

title: SPA, SSR or SSG? A Decision Tree
subtitle: The answer depends on SEO needs, data freshness and team capacity — not on what is fashionable.
takeaway: Framework migrations are expensive. Most authenticated products get more from a well-split SPA than from SSR.
prompt: Write a 3-4 bullet SPA vs SSR/SSG recommendation for this repo based on its routing and data fetching.

title: Prerendering Without a Framework Migration
subtitle: vite-ssg or vite-plugin-ssr can generate static HTML for selected routes while keeping the Vite SPA you already have.
takeaway: Incremental prerendering is the middle path: improve public-page SEO without rewriting the app around Nuxt.
prompt: Evaluate vite-ssg for this project's public routes and keep authenticated routes client-rendered.

title: Prefetch on Intent
subtitle: Fetch the next route while the user is still hovering or reading. Latency disappears before the click happens.
takeaway: Prefetching moves work into idle time. It is the last mile that makes lazy routes feel local.
prompt: Prefetch this next-likely route on hover/focus using requestIdleCallback or the router's prefetch hook.

title: Scaling Phase 1 Overview: Architecture & State
subtitle: Feature folders, composables, small stores and strict types turn one big app into independent, testable domains.
takeaway: Scaling is organizational before it is technical. The folder structure decides who can change what safely.
prompt: Refactor folder structure by feature/domain, extract use* composables, split Pinia stores and enable strict: true.

title: Feature-Sliced Design in Practice
subtitle: FSD orders layers so code only imports downward: app → pages → features → entities → shared.
takeaway: Layered dependencies make it obvious where a piece of code belongs and prevent circular imports by construction.
prompt: Map the current folders to these layers and move one feature into src/features/<domain>/ with a public index.ts.

title: Domain Feature Folders
subtitle: A feature folder owns its view, composable, API calls and types. Everything else imports its public index.
takeaway: Colocation makes the blast radius of a change visible and removes cross-team merge conflicts.
prompt: Move this feature's view, logic, API and types into one folder and expose only index.ts to the rest of the app.

title: Extract use<Feature> Composables
subtitle: A composable is a named unit of stateful logic you can test without mounting the DOM.
takeaway: Composables turn component logic into reusable, unit-testable modules while keeping the view declarative.
prompt: Extract stateful logic from this large .vue file into use<Feature>.ts and keep markup and bindings in the view.

title: Split Monolithic Pinia Stores
subtitle: One store per domain with Setup Store syntax keeps state, getters and actions together and independently testable.
takeaway: A single global store becomes a hidden dependency graph. Small stores make ownership and testing straightforward.
prompt: Split this monolithic store into single-responsibility Setup Stores and update feature imports to the new modules.

title: Strict TypeScript at Scale
subtitle: At scale, implicit any is a tax on every consumer. Strict types on stores and composables pay for themselves.
takeaway: Types are the interface between teams. Strictness makes a feature's contract visible before runtime.
prompt: Enable strict: true in tsconfig*.json and resolve implicit any in stores and composables first.

title: Migrate Folders Without Stopping the Product
subtitle: A big-bang restructure breaks everything. Move one domain at a time behind a stable public index.
takeaway: Migration risk is proportional to batch size. One domain per commit keeps the app shippable throughout.
prompt: Plan this folder migration as one domain per commit with vue-tsc and tests between each step.

title: Scaling Phase 2 Overview: Data Layer & Resilience
subtitle: Typed services, query caching, workers and error boundaries make the app resilient under real network and data loads.
takeaway: At scale, data bugs are usually about ownership: who caches, who retries, who handles failure. This phase assigns each.
prompt: Centralize fetch calls in typed services, introduce Vue Query, offload heavy transforms and wrap features in error boundaries.

title: Repository / Service Layer
subtitle: Components ask for domain data; a typed service knows the URL, mapping and error semantics.
takeaway: Centralized services make caching, auth headers and retries possible in one place instead of twenty components.
prompt: Move raw fetch/axios calls out of .vue files into typed src/services/<domain>.service.ts modules.

title: Shared HTTP Interceptors
subtitle: Auth headers, CSRF tokens, error normalization and 401 refresh belong in the client, not in every call site.
takeaway: Interceptors enforce consistent transport behaviour, which is especially important for security and observability.
prompt: Add shared request/response interceptors for credentials, CSRF headers and normalized errors in this HTTP client.

title: TanStack Query for Server State
subtitle: Server state has different needs from UI state: caching, deduplication, refetch on focus and stale time.
takeaway: Vue Query removes an entire category of loading, caching and invalidation code from components.
prompt: Introduce @tanstack/vue-query for this endpoint with a stable query key and a documented staleTime.

title: Request Deduplication
subtitle: Five components asking for the same key should cause one network request, not five.
takeaway: Dedup reduces server load and avoids flicker when several views mount at once.
prompt: Replace manual request guards here with a query key that all consumers share, and verify one network call.

title: Background Refetching
subtitle: Keep showing cached data while a fresh request runs. Use refetchOnWindowFocus and refetchInterval deliberately.
takeaway: Background refetching makes data fresh without making the UI blank — the same idea as stale-while-revalidate.
prompt: Configure staleTime and refetchOnWindowFocus for this query and keep cached data visible during refresh.

title: Offload Heavy Data Transforms
subtitle: Large CSV parsing or filtering belongs in a worker so the UI thread never freezes.
takeaway: Workers turn a main-thread freeze into a background task with a progress indicator.
prompt: Move this heavy parse/filter into a Vite worker, transfer the buffer and render progress from worker messages.

title: Error Boundaries at Feature Roots
subtitle: Wrap each major feature view so one widget's render error cannot blank the whole app.
takeaway: Boundaries turn total failures into local, recoverable ones — a requirement for large apps with many teams.
prompt: Wrap each major feature view in a reusable ErrorBoundary using onErrorCaptured with a retry fallback.

title: Scaling Phase 3 Overview: Governance & Delivery
subtitle: Design tokens, RBAC, budgets, CI checks and observability turn good intentions into automated guardrails.
takeaway: Governance is what makes the first two pillars survive the next ten developers and the next ten releases.
prompt: Consolidate design tokens, add meta-driven RBAC, set bundle budgets, run CI checks and add observability hooks.

title: Design Tokens in CSS Custom Properties
subtitle: One source for color, spacing and typography keeps every team's UI consistent and themes cheap.
takeaway: Tokens remove visual drift and make dark mode or rebranding a variable swap instead of a repository-wide edit.
prompt: Replace hardcoded colors, spacing and radii in this UI folder with CSS custom property design tokens.

title: Shared Component Library
subtitle: A small set of well-documented primitives with stable props and slots beats every team rebuilding a button.
takeaway: Shared UI raises the floor of quality across teams and reduces accessibility work to one implementation.
prompt: Consolidate duplicated buttons/inputs into src/shared/ui with typed props, slots and an index.ts export.

title: Meta-Driven RBAC Route Guards
subtitle: Permissions live on route meta and are enforced in router.beforeEach before a view ever mounts.
takeaway: Route-level permissions make access control declarative, reviewable and impossible to skip by deep-linking.
prompt: Add declarative role/permission meta to these routes and enforce it in router.beforeEach before mounting.

title: CI Gates: vue-tsc, Vitest, Playwright
subtitle: Automated checks are the only guardrail that runs when nobody is watching.
takeaway: CI turns conventions into enforcement. A pipeline with clear, fast failures keeps quality from depending on discipline.
prompt: Ensure CI runs vue-tsc, Vitest and Playwright plus the production build before any deploy.

title: Observability: Error & Performance Hooks
subtitle: Production feedback closes the loop: errors and long tasks should reach your dashboard, not the support inbox.
takeaway: You cannot optimize or secure what you cannot see. Hooks make production behaviour measurable.
prompt: Register app.config.errorHandler and Web Vitals reporting in src/main.ts with token/PII redaction.

title: Micro-Frontends: Decide With Data
subtitle: Module Federation solves independent deployment across teams. It also adds runtime and operational complexity.
takeaway: Federation is a last resort in the scaling roadmap. Start with module boundaries; escalate only when deployment ownership demands it.
prompt: Evaluate team size and deployment needs, then write a short recommendation on Module Federation for this repo.

title: Security Phase 1 Overview: XSS & Storage
subtitle: Sanitize at render boundaries, validate at input boundaries, and keep sensitive values out of the browser entirely.
takeaway: Most frontend security incidents start with untrusted text becoming executable code, or a secret becoming public.
prompt: Audit every v-html and dynamic :href, validate forms, scrub VITE_* secrets and remove tokens from storage and logs.

title: XSS Prevention Basics
subtitle: Vue escapes text by default. XSS appears when you opt out with v-html, dynamic attributes or raw DOM APIs.
takeaway: The attacker's input is data, never code. Keep it that way unless you have explicitly made it safe.
prompt: Find every v-html, innerHTML and dynamic :href in this component and classify it as sanitized or remove it.

title: Sanitize v-html With DOMPurify
subtitle: If you must render HTML, pass it through a battle-tested sanitizer before Vue inserts it.
takeaway: DOMPurify removes scripts, event handlers and javascript: URLs while preserving the formatting you intended.
prompt: Wrap this v-html binding in DOMPurify.sanitize with an explicit allowlist and add a regression test with an XSS payload.

title: Block javascript: URIs in Dynamic Links
subtitle: A dynamic :href can execute script when the value starts with javascript:. Allowlist safe protocols instead.
takeaway: Protocol validation is a small helper that closes a surprising number of injection paths.
prompt: Add a safeUrl() helper to this component's dynamic :href bindings and test it with a javascript: payload.

title: Schema Validation on User Forms
subtitle: Validate shape, length and type at the boundary with Zod or VeeValidate; never trust client values or API DTOs.
takeaway: A schema gives you a typed, validated value instead of an object full of assumptions.
prompt: Add a Zod schema to this form and submit only the parsed result, with inline errors for invalid fields.

title: Environment Variable Hygiene
subtitle: Everything named VITE_* is embedded in the client bundle. Secrets must never live there.
takeaway: There is no such thing as a private client-side environment variable. Move secrets behind a server endpoint.
prompt: Inspect .env* and import.meta.env.VITE_* usages here and remove any private key, token or database credential.

title: Redact Secrets in Logs & Errors
subtitle: console.log and error trackers often capture the whole request object — including tokens and PII.
takeaway: Logs are copied into tickets, dashboards and third-party tools; treat them as public storage.
prompt: Add a redaction helper to this logger/error reporter and remove token or PII dumps from console.log calls.

title: Storage Hygiene
subtitle: localStorage is readable by any script on the origin. Keep raw JWTs, passwords and PII out of it.
takeaway: Storage hygiene limits the blast radius of XSS and reduces privacy exposure on shared devices.
prompt: Remove raw tokens and PII from localStorage/sessionStorage in this feature and clear remaining keys on logout.

title: Security Phase 2 Overview: Auth & Headers
subtitle: Cookies, CSRF, RBAC, CSP and transport headers work together: no single one is sufficient.
takeaway: Security is defense in depth. Each layer assumes another one fails, so a single mistake is not a full compromise.
prompt: Harden cookie auth, CSRF, RBAC guards, CSP/frame-ancestors/HSTS, SRI, abuse controls and run npm audit.

title: HttpOnly Cookies for Sessions
subtitle: The browser sends the cookie automatically and JavaScript cannot read it — XSS no longer steals the session directly.
takeaway: HttpOnly removes the most valuable target from client-side script. It is the foundation of modern browser auth.
prompt: Configure the HTTP client with withCredentials: true and move token storage to an HttpOnly; Secure cookie.

title: Secure & SameSite Cookie Flags
subtitle: Secure blocks plain HTTP transmission; SameSite limits when the browser sends the cookie on cross-site requests.
takeaway: Cookie attributes are server configuration, not client code. Verify them in the browser's Application tab.
prompt: Set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite on the session cookie and verify the attributes in DevTools.

title: Safe 401 Refresh Rotation
subtitle: When an access token expires, rotate the refresh token once, replay the original request, and stop on a second failure.
takeaway: Naive refresh logic is a common source of retry storms and account lockouts. One refresh per failure is the rule.
prompt: Implement single-flight 401 refresh with a retry limit and logout on the second failure in this HTTP client.

title: CSRF Protection for State Changes
subtitle: Ambient cookies ride along on cross-site requests. Require an extra token that an attacker's site cannot read.
takeaway: CSRF tokens make the browser's automatic cookie behaviour safe for mutations.
prompt: Attach the CSRF header on every state-mutating request and confirm the server validates it.

title: RBAC Guards Before Mounting
subtitle: Client-side guards improve UX; the server must still authorize every request. Never rely on hiding a button.
takeaway: Route guards stop deep links to protected screens before they render and before their data requests fire.
prompt: Verify this router's beforeEach blocks unauthenticated and unauthorized navigation before the protected view mounts.

title: Content Security Policy
subtitle: CSP tells the browser which script, style, image and connect sources are allowed. Inline scripts become a thing of the past.
takeaway: CSP is the strongest browser-level defense against XSS and data exfiltration, but it needs careful rollout.
prompt: Add a strict CSP header in the hosting config, starting in Report-Only mode, and remove unsafe-inline where possible.

title: Clickjacking Protection
subtitle: Frame-ancestors in CSP (and X-Frame-Options as a fallback) stops attackers embedding your app in a transparent iframe.
takeaway: A one-line header removes an entire class of UI redressing attacks.
prompt: Set frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY in this app's hosting configuration.

title: Subresource Integrity for CDN Tags
subtitle: SRI makes the browser verify a hash before executing a third-party script. A compromised CDN cannot inject code.
takeaway: SRI protects the supply chain at the point of use, especially for scripts loaded from outside your build.
prompt: Add integrity and crossorigin attributes to every external script/style tag in index.html.

title: HTTPS & HSTS
subtitle: TLS protects data in transit; HSTS tells browsers to refuse plain HTTP for your domain in the future.
takeaway: HSTS turns a one-time redirect into a lasting guarantee that browsers will not fall back to HTTP.
prompt: Enforce HTTPS and add the HSTS header to this app's hosting config after verifying all subdomains.

title: Abuse Controls on Auth Forms
subtitle: Login, registration and password reset need throttling and bot checks to resist credential stuffing.
takeaway: Auth endpoints are public by definition. Rate limits make brute force economically pointless.
prompt: Add submit throttling and a CAPTCHA hook to these auth forms, plus server-side rate limits and 429 handling.

title: Dependency Vulnerability Auditing
subtitle: Your supply chain is code you did not write. Audit it in CI and upgrade high-severity advisories deliberately.
takeaway: A vulnerable transitive dependency is a vulnerability in your app. Continuous auditing makes that manageable.
prompt: Run npm audit --audit-level=high, report the advisories, and fix high-severity issues with tests re-run.

title: Verification 1: /frontend-opt-tests
subtitle: Prove that routes are lazy, heavy components load asynchronously, caching works and the production build is clean.
takeaway: This suite protects the user-visible work from being silently undone by later refactors.
prompt: Create Vitest tests in /frontend-opt-tests for lazy routes, async resolution, KeepAlive, computed caching, debounce and a clean build.

title: Verification 2: /scaling-tests
subtitle: Prove that services handle HTTP outcomes, state modules stay independent, and error boundaries contain crashes.
takeaway: Scaling changes touch many files; these tests are what make the refactor reversible and reviewable.
prompt: Create Vitest tests in /scaling-tests for service responses, deduplication, modular state and onErrorCaptured fallback UI.

title: Verification 3: /security-tests
subtitle: Prove that XSS payloads are stripped, guards block deep links, CSRF/credentials are attached and no secret leaks.
takeaway: Security tests are regression locks: they stop a future convenience change from reopening a closed hole.
prompt: Create Vitest regression tests in /security-tests for sanitization, RBAC redirects, CSRF, 401 refresh and storage/env hygiene, then run npm audit.

title: The Executive Summary
subtitle: One short report closes the pipeline: what changed, what passed, and what a human still must do.
takeaway: The summary is the handover artifact. It turns a long refactor into three paragraphs a reviewer can trust.
prompt: Write the executive summary with files modified per stage, all test results and the manual actions still required.

title: Before / After Scorecard
subtitle: Numbers make the story credible. Capture the same metrics before and after, on the same device and network settings.
takeaway: Optimization without measurement is opinion. A two-column scorecard turns the entire pipeline into evidence.
prompt: Record LCP, INP, CLS and bundle size before and after this phase under identical throttling, then commit the numbers.

title: The Roadmap Checklist
subtitle: Nine skills, three gates, one summary. This is the whole hardening pipeline on a single page.
takeaway: The checklist is the contract: one skill per session, a test gate per pillar, and a written handover at the end.
prompt: Follow the sequence 1-opt-1 → 1-opt-4 → 2-scale-1 → 2-scale-3 → 3-sec-1 → 3-sec-2 with a commit and a green suite between each step.
